description: Micron Technology, Inc. engages in the provision of semiconductor memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Mainland China, other Asia Pacific countries, Japan, Europe, and internation
description_full: Micron Technology, Inc. engages in the provision of semiconductor memory and storage products in the United States, Taiwan, Mainland China, other Asia Pacific countries, Japan, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Cloud Memory Business Unit, Core Data Center Business Unit, Mobile and Client Business Unit, and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit segments. The company provides dynamic random access memory (DRAM) products, including High-Bandwidth Memory, doublie data rate, low-power DRAM, and graphics DRAM products; NAND products comprising solid state drives, managed NAND, and multi-chip packages; and NOR products. The company sells its products under the Micron brand name and private labels through its own direct sales force, sales or representative offices, as well as through distributors, retailers, and independent sales representatives. Micron Technology, Inc. was founded in 1978 and is headquartered in Boise, Idaho.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 61K people. Revenue per employee of $2.2M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers, improving at 20%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $967K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $22K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: Micron Technology, Inc. is a mega-cap technology business with a $780.7B market cap on $133.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +105% over the past three years and +27% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +4.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 12% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 33%.

The business throws off $59.0B in free cash flow — roughly 44 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.06× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.2%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 75% operating margin runs 68pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+44.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 339% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 26% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 45% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 84% and a beta of 1.50, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 3.43 vs 5y 1.93), so read it loosely.

val: The stock trades 35% below its DCF fair value of $1,061, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 77%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $598 to $1,883 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 9.3 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 6.5 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 13.2 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 54% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 7.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 14.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 45 covering analysts target $1,562 on average, 126% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 16% earns above the cost of capital of 12.1%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.51).
It runs a 33% gross margin and converts 44% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.06x.
ROE of 61% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 50pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 4.2% of revenue on R&D and 1.0% on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $38.3B (4% of market cap).
Warning signs: a Beneish M-score that flags possible earnings manipulation, which caps the rating at HOLD.
Working capital ties up about 185 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 36.9% over 5 years and 26.8% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 70%).
At current returns, reinvesting 80% of profits supports about 12.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 89.1% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 2.00 (orders outpacing sales) and a backlog worth 1.0x annual revenue.
Capex runs 3.2x depreciation (23.1% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 80%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (121 sales, net $165.9M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.2% (0.1% in buybacks and 0.1% in dividends).
people: With about 61,000 employees, each generates about $2.2M of revenue, 5.9x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 19.9% a year.
That works out to $967K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $5.6M (3x revenue per employee).
